identity.name: Certificate-Fingerprint Infrastructure Pivot — GNN Surfaces a Self-Signed TLS Cert Reused Across Trident Ursa IPs (T1587.003)
identity.summary: A GNN over multi-feature infrastructure relationships is Unit 42's method; a reused self-signed TLS certificate fingerprint is one high-value pivot feature. The scenario arms the source's one certificate example — a Trident Ursa self-signed cert reused across multiple IPs — as the TIM pivot: a handshake fires the IOC match, the fingerprint fans out, and a rule stitches one incident.
identity.description: Unit 42's research applies a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to discover malicious infrastructure: from a small seed set of known-bad indicators the GNN learns relationships between network artifacts across MANY edge features — co-hosted domains, hosting duration, content structure, lexical patterns, malware-delivery URLs, C2 domains, and TLS certificate fingerprints — and pivots to surface additional related infrastructure. A self-signed TLS certificate fingerprint is ONE high-value edge feature among these: because generating a fresh certificate per host is operational friction adversaries often skip, the same self-signed certificate can appear on multiple IP addresses, stitching those hosts together even when no domain or IP overlaps. The report's single concrete certificate example is Russian actor Trident Ursa — multiple IP addresses hosting Trident Ursa content shared one self-signed certificate fingerprint (07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799). The report documents other, SEPARATE GNN-clustered infrastructure that is NOT linked by that certificate: an unattributed postal/package-delivery phishing network (correosesllr[.]top, inposdomag[.]top, usps.postscy[.]top co-hosted on 47.251.0[.]168, with reuse hub 146.112.61[.]108 hosting ~160 domains) surfaced via shared HOSTING; an unattributed web-skimming set (apple.com-ticket[.]info, ssl-google-analytics[.]com) whose indicators partially overlap with activity previously attributed to TA569; and a Squeamish Libra / FIN7 scanner-lookalike set (advanced-ip-sccanner[.]com) distributing a fake Advanced IP Scanner installer. This TIM-plane scenario reproduces the ONE genuine certificate-fingerprint pivot in a lab: mocktaxii arms the Trident Ursa self-signed certificate fingerprint as the pivot indicator; an estate host performs TLS handshakes to lab hosts that present that shared self-signed certificate (the NGFW captures tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1); Cortex raises a TIM IOC match on the certificate fingerprint and then fans out on the shared fingerprint to roll up every co-fingerprinted IP the estate touched. A correlation rule gates on the feed-presence of the certificate indicator and joins the self-signed-cert BIOC to the fingerprint fan-out on the shared tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 into one Resource-Development adversary-infrastructure incident. The point is that a reused certificate fingerprint is a high-fidelity pivot FEATURE — one of several the GNN weighs — not the sole method, and not a link across the otherwise-unrelated postal, skimming, and scanner clusters.

campaigns: Trident Ursa self-signed TLS certificate (07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799) reused across multiple IP addresses — Unit 42 GNN infrastructure discovery (2022-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-TIM-004 — Certificate-fingerprint infrastructure pivot on the TIM plane (defender-vantage; mocktaxii-armed self-signed certificate fingerprint reused across multiple IPs).

prerequisites.description: mocktaxii TAXII 2.1 collection reachable so the self-signed certificate fingerprint indicator (the pivot key) is ingested into the XSIAM threat_intel dataset.
NGFW / decryption telemetry captures the server certificate fingerprint (tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1) on TLS handshakes from the estate so the pivot has a field to fan out on.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE / NON-DESTRUCTIVE. No exploitation, no payload delivery. Perform TLS
# handshakes to several lab hosts that all present the ONE shared self-signed
# certificate (Trident Ursa fingerprint 07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799)
# and READ the server certificate fingerprint so the NGFW/network telemetry sees
# the same fingerprint fan out across multiple destination IPs.
set -euo pipefail
ZONE="${TIM_ZONE:-cortexsim-tim.internal}"
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] SIM-TIM-004 certificate-fingerprint pivot against lab zone ${ZONE}"
for host in "tu-node-a.${ZONE}" "tu-node-b.${ZONE}" "tu-node-c.${ZONE}"; do
  echo | timeout 5 openssl s_client -connect "${host}:443" -servername "${host}" 2>/dev/null \
    | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha1 2>/dev/null || true
done
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-TIM-004 handshake sweep complete — one cert fingerprint observed across the lab IPs for the fan-out roll-up.'

input_variables.name: TIM_ZONE
input_variables.description: Authorised lab DNS zone whose hosts present the shared SAFE-MODE self-signed certificate the pivot fans out on.

expected_artifacts.description: TLS handshakes from the estate host to multiple lab hosts that all present the same self-signed server certificate fingerprint.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: tls_cert_self_signed = true and tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 = "07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799" shared across >= 2 distinct dst_ip

expected_artifacts.description: TIM IOC match on the armed self-signed certificate fingerprint captured on the estate handshake.

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-TIM-004 cleanup complete — no artifacts written (read-only handshakes).'

iocs.context: Self-signed TLS certificate SHA-1 fingerprint reused across multiple Trident Ursa IP addresses (Unit 42 GNN research). THE certificate-fingerprint pivot anchor — the only concrete certificate indicator the source documents. Armed in TIM as a CERT_FINGERPRINT / TLS_CERT_SHA1 indicator; the BIOC and fan-out XQL key on this value.

Postal/package-delivery phishing hosting hub — serves look-alike domains (correosesllr[.]top, inposdomag[.]top, usps.postscy[.]top). Unattributed in the source. A SEPARATE GNN cluster surfaced via shared HOSTING, NOT tied to the certificate fingerprint. Documentary IOC breadth.

Long-lived infrastructure-reuse hub — ~160 malicious domains over the prior year (Unit 42). Unattributed. A GNN hosting-duration / shared-hosting pivot feature, NOT a certificate pivot. Documentary IOC breadth.
Postal/delivery look-alike phishing domain co-hosted on 47.251.0.168. Unattributed. Surfaced by the GNN via shared hosting, not by any shared certificate.
Postal/delivery look-alike phishing domain in the shared-hosting postal cluster on 47.251.0.168. Unattributed. Not certificate-linked.
USPS look-alike phishing domain in the shared-hosting postal cluster on 47.251.0.168. Unattributed. Not certificate-linked.
Web-skimming exfiltration domain. Attribution unclear; some indicators overlap with activity previously attributed to TA569 (Unit 42). A GNN content/lexical cluster, not certificate-linked.
Web-skimming exfiltration domain masquerading as Google Analytics. Attribution unclear (possible TA569 overlap per Unit 42). Not certificate-linked.

Scanner-lookalike malware-distribution domain hosting a fake Advanced_Ip_Scanner_setup.exe (Carbanak/Aranuk installer). Attributed to Squeamish Libra / FIN7 (Unit 42). A separate GNN cluster, not certificate-linked.

biocs.name: SIM-TIM-004 Estate Handshake to a TIM-Armed Self-Signed Certificate
biocs.description: An estate host completes a TLS handshake to a destination presenting the mocktaxii-armed self-signed certificate — server-certificate fingerprint equals the feed-armed value 07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799. Keying on the armed fingerprint (not a broad self-signed-cert predicate and not any single domain) is what seeds the fingerprint fan-out; a default/snakeoil self-signed cert cannot match, so there is no false-positive breadth.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app = "ssl" or app = "web-browsing"
| filter tls_cert_self_signed = true and tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 = "07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799"
| comp count() as handshakes by agent_hostname, src_host, dst_ip, dst_host, tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1
| filter handshakes >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, src_host, dst_ip, dst_host, tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1, handshakes

xql_queries.name: SIM-TIM-004 Cert-Fingerprint Indicator Ingested
xql_queries.query:
dataset = threat_intel
| filter indicator_type in ("CERT_FINGERPRINT", "TLS_CERT_SHA1")
| filter indicator_value = "07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799"
| filter reference contains "certificate-fingerprint-pivot"
| comp count() as armed_indicators by indicator_type, indicator_value
| filter armed_indicators >= 1
| fields indicator_type, indicator_value, armed_indicators

xql_queries.name: SIM-TIM-004 Shared Self-Signed Cert Fingerprint Fan-Out Across IPs
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app = "ssl" or app = "web-browsing"
| filter tls_cert_self_signed = true and tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 = "07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799"
| comp count_distinct(dst_ip) as distinct_ips, count_distinct(dst_host) as distinct_domains by tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1
| filter distinct_ips >= 2
| sort desc distinct_ips
| fields tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1, distinct_ips, distinct_domains

xql_queries.name: SIM-TIM-004 Feed Match Stitched to TLS Handshake on Cert Fingerprint
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter tls_cert_self_signed = true and tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 = "07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799"
| comp count() as cluster_sessions, count_distinct(dst_ip) as cluster_ips by tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1, src_host
| filter cluster_sessions >= 1
| fields tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1, src_host, cluster_sessions, cluster_ips

correlation_rules.name: SIM-TIM-004 Certificate-Fingerprint Infrastructure-Cluster Incident
correlation_rules.logic: GATE XQL(SIM-TIM-004 Cert-Fingerprint Indicator Ingested) — a feed-presence precondition confirming the self-signed certificate fingerprint is armed in threat_intel (it is not a join participant). JOIN BIOC(SIM-TIM-004 Estate Handshake to a TIM-Armed Self-Signed Certificate) with XQL(SIM-TIM-004 Shared Self-Signed Cert Fingerprint Fan-Out Across IPs) on the shared tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 entity within the correlation window — both carry that key. Together they fuse the certificate-fingerprint IOC match with the multi-IP fingerprint fan-out into one Resource-Development adversary-infrastructure incident scoped to the shared certificate. The incident rolls up every co-fingerprinted IP the estate touched under that one fingerprint.

threat_scenarios.name: Certificate-Fingerprint Infrastructure-Cluster Pivot on the TIM Plane
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex TIM arms the source-documented self-signed TLS certificate fingerprint (a Trident Ursa cert reused across multiple IPs) as the pivot indicator; a matching estate handshake raises an IOC hit and the fingerprint fan-out rolls up every co-fingerprinted IP into one Resource-Development adversary-infrastructure incident.

threat_steps.objective: The TIM-armed self-signed certificate fingerprint plus an estate handshake to a host presenting that certificate raises the certificate-fingerprint IOC match and the estate-handshake BIOC.
preconditions: mocktaxii armed the self-signed certificate fingerprint (07eee6e893766e8bcc4a711abfdf201ee2920799) into threat_intel.
NGFW/decryption telemetry captures tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 on the handshake.
steps: Confirm the cert-fingerprint indicator set is ingested.
Perform a TLS handshake from the estate host to a lab host presenting the armed self-signed certificate.
Observe the TIM IOC match and the estate-handshake BIOC fire.
success_criteria: XQL `SIM-TIM-004 Cert-Fingerprint Indicator Ingested` returns the armed indicator set.
BIOC `SIM-TIM-004 Estate Handshake to a TIM-Armed Self-Signed Certificate` fires on the handshake.

threat_steps.objective: The armed certificate fingerprint fans out across >= 2 distinct destination IPs, rolling up the co-fingerprinted hosts.
preconditions: Estate handshakes to multiple lab hosts presenting the armed self-signed certificate recorded in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw.
steps: Run the fingerprint fan-out hunt query over the handshake window.
Confirm one fingerprint groups multiple distinct destinations.
success_criteria: XQL `SIM-TIM-004 Shared Self-Signed Cert Fingerprint Fan-Out Across IPs` returns the armed fingerprint with distinct_ips >= 2.

threat_steps.objective: The correlation rule fuses the feed match and the fingerprint fan-out into one Resource-Development infrastructure-cluster incident scoped to the shared certificate.
preconditions: The feed match and fan-out both observed on the shared tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 within the correlation window.
steps: Confirm the incident rolls up every co-fingerprinted IP the estate touched.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-TIM-0004` raises exactly one Resource-Development adversary-infrastructure incident.
The incident is scoped to the shared certificate fingerprint and enumerates the co-fingerprinted IPs.

preventive_controls: Block TLS sessions to hosts presenting self-signed certificates whose fingerprints are on a threat-intel indicator list at the NGFW.
Enforce decryption on egress so the firewall can observe server-certificate fingerprints rather than only SNI/domain.
Subscribe TIM to certificate-fingerprint indicators (not only domain/IP) so provisioned-infrastructure reuse is caught before a domain is even blocked.
detection_engineering: Arm the certificate fingerprint — not a single domain — as the TIM pivot indicator; a self-signed thumbprint reused across IPs is a higher-fidelity cluster anchor than any one domain.

Alert only when a FEED-MATCHED self-signed certificate fingerprint (one on a threat-intel indicator list) is observed across two or more distinct destination IPs. Do NOT alert on any self-signed fingerprint shared across destinations — default/snakeoil certs (Ubuntu ssl-cert-snakeoil, k8s ingress default, appliance/load-balancer/IoT defaults) are shared byte-for-byte across many internal hosts, so an unqualified 'one fingerprint across >= 2 destinations' rule pages the SOC continuously. Exclude RFC1918 destinations and maintain a known-good self-signed-cert allowlist.
Stitch the TIM feed match to the NGFW fingerprint fan-out on tls_cert_fingerprint_sha1 into a single Resource-Development cluster incident rather than N per-IP alerts.
